speaker: abel_garnish
text: I stopped at fifteen. I will not stand in that yard and count a sixteenth.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Fifteen what, Master Garnish? If you mean laughs, fifteen is a poor afternoon, and I have not done. The slippers came after, and they would not let me go.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou fed them, Will, and they ate. A holiday yard. Let it be a holiday yard.

speaker: margery_pell
text: I emptied the box. I have not my line for you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then give us the other thing. What was the yard, before the jig?

speaker: margery_pell
text: 'Prentices thick as flies, and no good humour in them. They laughed like men who mean to laugh at something else after.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: They laughed. That is the trade. I shrug it off.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I do not.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You never do, when the laugh is not the one you wrote. The messenger could not get his hush. It came late, and it broke early, and the scene had a hole, and I stood in the hole.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The hush is written. It is a still yard, Master Kemp, not a drum. They broke it, and at fifteen I stopped. I am not counting your lines.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fifteen is enough to know. More apprentices than sweethearts. Loud before we began, and loud in it. The biggest yard since Easter Monday, and not the same kind of big.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Easter Monday came to be merry. Thou art making a chronicle of a Whit Monday. Thou playedst the comedy. The comedy was played.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not making a chronicle. I am telling thee I heard them.

speaker: margery_pell
text: The stair was the same as the yard. Caps on, and nobody asking the title. They knew what they had come to stand in.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And they had me. The jig of the slippers. They would not let me go. I am not a man who refuses a yard that knows its mind. By my hose, loud is not a sin on a holiday.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The book knows its mind. The jig is after the book. I have nothing to say to slippers, Master Kemp.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Peace, Abel. The book will be as it was at noon. No one is rewriting the comedy in the tiring-house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not rewriting it. I am not shrugging it either.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Then take it home, if you must have it. I am for a drink, and I am not for a sermon. You may keep the fifteen. I am keeping the yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Loud is not the point. The humour is. She said it. No good humour in them.

speaker: margery_pell
text: I said it. I will not say the box. Not today. Do not ask me for the line I did not bring.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Master Will, the messenger's hush. If you will mend it, mend it in the margin, and I will copy the margin. I will not have it mended by a jig.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not mend it tonight. The hush stands. They would not keep it. That is a different fault from a line.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then we are done. Thou hast thy disagreement, and I have a dry throat, and the flag is down. Come, Will. Leave him the fifteen.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Fifteen, and the slippers, and a yard that would not let me off. Write that in your table if you write anything. You may have it for nothing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have it. Go on. I am not behind you.

speaker: margery_pell
text: The stair is clear. That is the best of the day, and it is the only best I have.
